title: Inflation

objectives.text: Explain inflation as a rise in the price of goods and services over time.
Calculate a real return by subtracting inflation from a nominal return.
Explain why cash held idle loses purchasing power.

explanation: Inflation is the rate at which prices of goods and services rise over a period. If a kilogram of apples costs ₹100 this year and ₹110 next year, prices rose by ₹10, which is 10%. The same money buys less, so the cost of living goes up.

What matters is the real return, not the headline return. RBI's FAME material defines it simply as return percentage minus inflation percentage. Money in a deposit earning 6% while inflation is 4% has a real return of 2%. Money held as cash earns 0%, so with 4% inflation its real return is minus 4%.

This is why idle cash is not neutral. It feels safe because the number does not fall, but its purchasing power does. Savings and investments need a return at least above inflation to preserve what the money can buy over the years.

examples.title: Real return on a deposit
examples.text: Meera keeps ₹50,000 in a deposit earning 6% a year while inflation is 4%. Her real return is 2%. On ₹50,000 that is roughly ₹1,000 of real gain for the year, not the ₹3,000 the headline rate suggests.

examples.title: Cash under the mattress
examples.text: Rahul keeps ₹20,000 as cash at home for a year. The note count is unchanged, but with 4% inflation those rupees buy about 4% less, a real loss of roughly ₹800 in purchasing power.

keyTakeaways: Inflation is a rise in prices, so the same money buys less over time.
Real return is the return percentage minus the inflation percentage.
Cash earning nothing has a negative real return whenever prices rise.
Aim for returns above inflation to preserve purchasing power.

review.notes: Definition, the apples example and the real-return formula are checked against RBI FAME 4th edition, Message 8. No current inflation rate is quoted, since rates change. Awaiting a named human reviewer.

quiz.question: A kilogram of apples goes from ₹100 to ₹110 in a year. What happened?
quiz.explanation: A ₹10 rise on a ₹100 base is a 10% increase, which is the inflation rate for that item over the year.

quiz.question: Your deposit earns 6% while inflation is 4%. What is the real return?
quiz.explanation: RBI's FAME material calculates real return as return minus inflation: 6% minus 4% equals 2%.

quiz.question: Why does cash kept idle lose value?
options: Because prices rise while the cash earns nothing
Because banks charge a fee on cash at home
quiz.explanation: The cash earns a 0% return, so with positive inflation its real return is negative and it buys less over time.

disclaimer: General financial education, not personalised advice. Inflation varies by item and over time; no current rate is quoted here.
